timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, my name is David Onig. I'm a criminal justice attorney running for district attorney
to make San Francisco the safest and fairest city in the country. I'm running for district
attorney because our criminal justice system is completely broken. We're spending so
much on our prisons that we have practically bankrupted the state. At the same time,
seven out of ten people who come out of prison return within three years. We need to dramatically
overhaul the system to make our community safer. We need a DA who knows how to reform the system
so it works more fairly and more effectively, and that's exactly what I've been doing for
the past 20 years. I started my career at Walden House, counseling delinquent kids and helping
them turn their lives around. At the National Council on Crime and Delinquency, I helped
write the book for the Clinton Justice Department on alternatives to incarceration. After graduating
from Stanford Law School, I worked at legal services for children, providing free legal
services to low-income kids. At the W. Haywood Burns Institute, I worked to reduce racial
disparities in the juvenile justice system. At the mayor's office of criminal justice and on the San
Francisco Police Commission, I helped bring national best practices to San Francisco law enforcement.
Finally, I founded the Berkeley Center for Criminal Justice with a mission of bringing law
enforcement and community together to build collaboration around pragmatic criminal justice reform.
That is what my whole career has been about, and that is what this whole campaign is about.
I've been reforming the system from the outside for the past 20 years, and now I want to keep
reforming the system as your next district attorney. I will reform the system by focusing on what
prevents crime, intervening early with youth to keep them in school and out of the criminal justice
system, never seeking the death penalty under any circumstances, because the data shows it
doesn't make us safer. Reforming three strikes so that it focuses on the violent offenders we
need to keep off our streets to protect public safety. I have been endorsed by an incredibly
diverse coalition of over 2,000 supporters, including Sheriff Michael Hennessy, former police chiefs,
Heather Fong and Tony Rivera, the California Police Chiefs Association, and over 30 current and
former members of the San Francisco Police Department. Education leaders like United Educators of
San Francisco and the vast majority of the San Francisco School Board, community leaders from
every neighborhood of the city, as well as the San Francisco Democratic Party, the Harvey Milk Club,
the League of Conservation Voters, and many others. This diverse group has come together to support
my campaign because they all know our criminal justice system is broken, and they hunger for reform,
and they know that I am the candidate with the proven record of delivering reform from the outside.
Again, I'm David Onik, and I'm running for district attorney. Please join us and learn more at
davidonik.com. Thank you.
